headline: Approved the Mission Statement with September's changes and tabled the Unattended Child Policy to the next meeting.
summary: The meeting covered library finances, staffing, programming, and budget advocacy. Members approved the Mission Statement. The Unattended Child Policy was tabled to the next meeting.
decisions: Approved the Mission Statement with the changes made at the September meeting. All members were in favor.
Tabled the Unattended Child Policy to the next meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: After discussion, all Board members were in favor of approving the Mission Statement with the changes that were made in September's meeting.
Unattended Child Policy Tabled to the next meeting.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Library Board Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, October 13, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
Second Floor 
Conference Room 
2700 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 Pat Sirulnick called the meeting to order at 6:08pm. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 In Person: Pat Sirulnick, Melissa Canham - Clyne, Phil Kuchuk, Amber Woodward, Jan 
Glover, Anita 
Online: Brett Prestia, Zac Zuber Zander, Marcia Romanski, Alyssa Danshinghani 
3. ADDITIONS TO THE AGENDA 
  
 No additions to the agenda. 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  a. September 8th, 2026  
  
• Pat noted that the December meeting date is 12.14.26 not  12.06.26. 
• Jan Glover made a motion to approve the minutes with the corrections stated 
by Pat. Phil seconded the motion. 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Melissa Canham-Clyne read a letter from a school expressing gratitude for the amount of 
books their students received. 
6. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 No public comment.
7. ADMINISTRATIVE REPORTS 
  
 Melissa Canham-Clyne reviewed the Library Administration report and financials for the 
upcoming Trustee meeting on Tuesday, Oct 13.library community is trying to work with the 
publishing industry to change the way libraries purchase ebooks 
• Ebooks can only be leased at the moment. 
• Decrease in personnel salaries due to changes in staff 
o retirement vs entry level new hires 
• Increase in programming 
o Better accounting put towards programming 
• Increase in cost of delivered goods, decrease in quality of delivery 
o Possible course of action: stop deliveries from private vendor and ask state 
to take over 
Alyssa reported on: 
• Staffing 
o Down 22% 
o Hiring for Branch Manager and Librarian One position is moving forward 
• Programming 
o 24 adult programs in September 
o 208 teens brought in for the teen department 
• Online traction through social media posts 
 
8. MEET THE STAFF 
  
 No new staff to meet. 
9. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
  
 
 
  a. FOHL Liaison 
 
 
 
  
  Anita gave updates on Friends of the Library Week. 
• Envelope fundraiser at the library 
• Fundraising at Chipotle  
• Tabling at the library to encourage membership 
• Library advocacy on the Green 
 
  b. Personal Board-related Goals  
  Pat talked about goals in regard to advocating for the library.
• The Commission took turns talking about their goals 
• Marcia spoke in depth about different advocacy projects that include fun facts 
from the Administrative Reports 
 
10. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  a. Financial update 
 
 
 
  
  
• Melissa reviewed:  
o The Legislative council passed a rule that only a certain amount of 
money can be transferred through the town and its entities on a 
quarterly basis. It appears to be 1st come 1st serve basis. 15K cap for 
the whole town. 
o Zac provided some clarification of the rule: 15k/quater w/o Legislative 
Council approval 
o Brett proposed setting up a recurring monthly outreach to preemptively 
get on the agenda for the Legislative Council. 
o The Board discussed concerns at large. 
 
 
• Gift Fund Report: got a lot of money, spent a lot of money 
o Large donation from Wilder Foundation 
o Donation from the Friends to support Fall programming 
o Whitneyville Plants  
o Melissa reviewed administrative expenses 
• MUNIS Report: 
o Transfer money into overtime 
o Reducing Library hours for a more sustainable work schedule for staff 
• The Board discussed the backlog from staff reduction  
• Closed on Thanksgiving and Black Friday 
 
  b. Committee Reports  
 
  
  
 
  i. Finance 
 
  
  Phil reported that financially, the Board is ahead of all his projections.
ii. Strategic Focus 
 
 
       
  Melissa gave updates: 
• Committee meeting at 9:30am on 10.14.26 
• Note takers needed 
• Surveyors needed 
 
  c. Mission Statement  
 
  
  
• Pat reviewed changes from last meeting 
• Jan Glover made a motion to approve the Mission Statement created by the 
Board.  
o Amber seconded the motion.  
o Pat asked if there was any discussion.  
o Marcia proposed the misnomer Library Board of Trustees be named 
the Library Board.  
▪ The Board at large disagreed with that change based on how 
the state of Connecticut views the entity.  
• After discussion, all Board members were in favor of approving the Mission 
Statement with the changes that were made in September's meeting. 
 
  d. Unattended Child Policy   
  Tabled to the next meeting. 
11. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  a. Budget Advocacy   
  Melissa reported on Budget Advocacy and ways to advocate for the library: 
• Soft touch examle: Zac Zander Zuber asking an acquaintance of the legislative 
council for clarification on the new budget rule that just passed 
• 8 touches for change 
 
12. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommend by town attorney)  
 No executive session needed. 
13. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 Phil made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Amber seconded the motion. The meeting 
adjourned at 7:42pm.
